doc.title: Warren Bernhardt interviewed by Monk Rowe, Bearsville, New York, January 3, 2012

title: Working on the Rachmaninoff Rhapsody
summary: He is memorizing the Paganini Rhapsody and listens only to Rachmaninoff's own recording.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I’m working pretty much full time on this Rachmaninoff Rhapsody. It takes that kind of concentration. I’ve got it pretty well memorized now, but now the execution of it is very high level. So it’s just going to take a lot of work.
Do you put recordings of it on and listen to it a lot or do you find it’s not that helpful?

If I see a note that I think is wrong I’ll listen. I’ll only listen to the Rachmaninoff version, with him playing. Because the intent and the — the whole, what’s the shape of this thing? What’s the point of it? And I’m still trying to find the point in that piece. Like what’s the point that you’re reaching in that 24 minute piece that makes — what’s the point of doing it? There’s one moment in there, for you, only for you to find it. And you either make the point or you miss the point.
It sounds like high pressure. Of course why should it be easy?
God is prescient isn’t it? Haven’t I heard it somewhere?
